Payment reminder emails for overdue invoices (examples to copy)

Chasing money is awkward, so it gets put off. A fixed schedule and ready wording take the awkwardness out of it.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: send a payment reminder email at four points: a note a few days before the due date, a friendly one a few days after, a firmer one about two weeks late, and a final notice at around 30 days. Every email carries the invoice number, amount, due date, the invoice attached, and one clear way to pay. Copyable examples for each step are below.

What a payment reminder email looks like

Often a late payment is forgetfulness or a lost invoice, not refusal. Write the early emails as if that is the case. Then get a little firmer only if you hear nothing.

The format

Subject line. Put the invoice number and the amount or the status in it, so it is clear and easy to find later. "Invoice 1042 was due on March 3" works better than "Reminder" or "Just checking in." Leave out all-caps and warnings in the early emails.

Every reminder needs the same five things:

  1. The invoice number and what the work or goods were.
  2. The amount owed.
  3. The due date (and, once it is late, the number of days overdue).
  4. How to pay.
  5. Who to contact, by name, with a phone number.

Attach the invoice every time, as a PDF, so the customer does not have to search their inbox. Give one clear way to pay. A single pay link is best. If you list a link, a check address and bank details all at once, people stall. Offer a second option only in the later emails, if a customer says the link does not work for them.

Keep it short. Four or five sentences is enough. Add the tone with one line, not a paragraph.

When to send each one

  1. Before the due date (optional): 3 to 7 days ahead, for large invoices or customers who are often late.
  2. 3 to 7 days late: a friendly nudge.
  3. About 14 days late: a firmer reminder that asks for a payment date.
  4. About 30 days late: a final notice that says what happens next.

For more on timing, see how often to send invoice reminders. After the final notice, pick up the phone. A call often settles in two minutes what three emails could not.

Payment reminder email examples

1. Before the due date

This is a courtesy note, not a chase. It is the easiest one to send and it often heads off a late payment.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due [due date] Hi [name], Thanks for your business. This is a reminder that invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due on [due date]. The invoice is attached. You can pay online here: [pay link] If you have already arranged payment, thank you. [your name] [business name], [phone]

2. Just overdue: a friendly email to the customer

Use this for a past due invoice email to a customer who has simply missed it. Do not apologize for asking, and do not accuse.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] was due on [due date] Hi [name], I'm checking in because invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date] and I don't see a payment yet. I've attached a copy in case the first one got lost. You can pay here: [pay link] If it's already on its way, thank you, and please ignore this. If anything on the invoice looks wrong, tell me and I'll fix it. [your name]

3. Firmer reminder

Use this when the first nudge got no answer. It asks for a specific reply date and leaves room for a problem.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is now [days] days overdue Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date], and we haven't received payment or heard back. A copy is attached. Could you reply by [reply date] and tell me when we can expect payment? If there's a problem with the invoice, or you need to split the amount, tell me and we'll work something out. You can pay here: [pay link] [your name] [phone]

4. Final notice

This is the overdue payment email to send once friendlier tries have failed. State a date and one consequence you are entitled to and willing to carry out. Late fees and collection rules differ by state and by your agreement with the customer, so check your own terms first. This is not legal advice.

Subject: Final notice: invoice [invoice number], [amount] Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is now [days] days overdue, and I haven't had a reply to my earlier reminders. Please pay by [final date]. If we don't have payment or hear from you by then, we will [pause further work / add the late fee in our terms / pass the account on for collection]. You can pay here: [pay link]. If something has gone wrong on your side, call me on [phone] and we can agree a plan. [your name] [business name]

A late payment letter to a customer

Some customers, such as property managers, government offices and older businesses, still expect a formal letter. A letter is also useful as a PDF attachment on a final notice, because it gives you a dated record. It is the same message as the email, with the formal parts added: addresses, a date, a reference line and a clear deadline.

[Your business name] [Your address] [Phone] | [Email] [Date] [Customer name] [Customer business name, if any] [Customer address] Re: Overdue invoice [invoice number], [amount] Dear [name], Our records show that invoice [invoice number], dated [invoice date], for [amount] was due on [due date] and remains unpaid. The invoice covers [what the work or goods were]. A copy is enclosed. Please pay the balance of [amount] by [final date]. You can pay by [pay link / check made out to business name and mailed to the address above / bank transfer using the details on the invoice]. If you have already paid, please send me the date and method so I can match it. If you dispute any part of the invoice, please write or call me by [reply date] so we can resolve it. [If your agreement allows: Under our terms dated [terms date], a late fee of [late fee] applies to balances unpaid after [days] days.] Sincerely, [your name] [your title], [business name]

Send it by mail, or attach it as a PDF to a short email that says "Please see the attached letter regarding invoice [invoice number]." Keep a copy. Only include the late fee line if your signed agreement or invoice terms actually allow it.

Sending them without the hassle

You can send all of these by hand from your own email, using a saved template for each stage. The weak point is not the writing. It is remembering who is due which reminder and checking they have not paid. A short list kept in a spreadsheet, with the invoice number, due date and date of the last reminder, is enough to keep track. If you use QuickBooks Online, see how to automate invoice reminders in QuickBooks Online.

Mistakes to avoid

  • Chasing someone who has paid. Check for payments that arrived that morning before you send.
  • Chasing a customer mid-dispute or on a payment plan. Keep a short list of people who are never sent the standard reminder.
  • Sending two reminders in the same week because two people in the office both thought it was their job.
  • Threatening something you will not do. If you will not send it to collections, do not say you will.
